profile.summary: S3F-MSA is not a separate network: it is S3F ensembled with predictions from EVE, an alignment-based model, by adding the two models' z-scores. S3F (Sequence-Structure-Surface Fitness model) predicts how amino acid substitutions change protein fitness without training on any fitness data. It combines per-residue outputs of the ESM-2-650M protein language model with a graph network over the protein backbone structure and a second network over the protein surface, represented as a point cloud. The input is a wild-type sequence, its predicted structure, and the mutants to score; the EVE part also needs a multiple sequence alignment. The output is one score per mutant.

*Sequence-Structure-Surface Fitness Model (**S3F**)* is a novel multimodal representation learning framework that integrates protein features across several scales.
which enhances S2F by adding a protein surface encoder that represents surfaces as point clouds and facilitates message passing between neighboring points.
S2F utilizes the output of the protein language model as node features

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: S2F builds a radius graph over alpha carbons (edges under 10 Å) and runs Geometric Vector Perceptron (GVP) message passing, starting from ESM-2-650M embeddings as node features. The paper gives 5 GVP layers with 100 scalar and 16 vector hidden features; the released s2f.yaml config sets node_h_dim to [256, 16]. S3F adds a surface encoder: dMaSIF generates a surface point cloud from the backbone, each point is linked to its 16 nearest surface neighbours, and residue and surface features are exchanged through the 20 nearest surface points of each residue. Pre-training predicts masked residue types on 30,948 CATH v4.3.0 structures with ESM-2-650M frozen, so only the GVP layers are trained. At inference, mutation sites are masked; for residues with AlphaFold2 pLDDT below 70 the ESM-2-650M score is used instead. For S3F-MSA, the S3F score is then combined with the EVE score by summing z-scores.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository and Zenodo record 14257708 (published 2024-12-02) provide two checkpoints: s2f.pth (2,684,305,563 bytes) and s3f.pth (2,844,210,889 bytes). S3F-MSA uses s3f.pth. Both also need the ESM-2-650M weights (esm2_t33_650M_UR50D.pt). No S3F-MSA checkpoint or ensembling script is released: the repository's scripts cover pre-training, surface processing and S3F evaluation only, so a S3F-MSA result also depends on which EVE scores were used. A result should name the checkpoint file, the commit of the code and the structures used.

sections.title: What distinguishes S3F-MSA
sections.body: S3F-MSA is the alignment-augmented form of S3F. The authors built it to compare against alignment-based models; it needs an MSA and EVE predictions for each protein, which plain S3F does not.

quotes.text: To benchmark against alignmentbased models, we further enhance our models by ensembling them with EVE predictions
ensembling them with EVE predictions through the summation of their z-scores, resulting in two variants named S2F-MSA and S3F-MSA.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Ensemble of S3F with the alignment-based EVE model; zero-shot protein fitness predictor that adds structure and surface encoders to a frozen protein language model.

quotes.text: ensembling them with EVE predictions through the summation of their z-scores, resulting in two variants named S2F-MSA and S3F-MSA.

During pre-training, the weights of the ESM2-650M model are frozen, and only the GVP layers for structure and surface graphs are trainable.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: ESM-2-650M embeddings as node features for 5 GVP message-passing layers over a 10 Å alpha-carbon radius graph; a second GVP network over a dMaSIF surface point cloud. Hidden sizes differ between paper (100 scalar, 16 vector) and released config ([256, 16]).

quotes.text: Practically, we utilize L = 5 layers of GVP, with d′ = 16 vector and d = 100 scalar hidden representations.
node_h_dim: [256, 16]
class: SurfGVP

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Wild-type sequence and its predicted structure (AlphaFold2 structures in the paper and README) plus the substitutions to score, plus surface graphs computed from the structure, plus EVE predictions, which need an MSA.

quotes.text: We use AlphaFold2 to predict the wild-type structures.

ensembling them with EVE predictions through the summation of their z-scores, resulting in two variants named S2F-MSA and S3F-MSA.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: One fitness score per mutant. The evaluation script writes output files to ~/scratch/proteingym_output, set by output_dir in the config.

quotes.text: The output files can be found at `~/scratch/proteingym_output`, which is specified by the `output_dir` argument in the `*.yaml`.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 260M trainable parameters for S3F-MSA, as listed in the paper's Table 1. ESM-2-650M is frozen inside the model and is not counted as trainable. For the ensemble the figure includes the EVE part, which the paper estimates for an average sequence length of 400.

quotes.text: During pre-training, the weights of the ESM2-650M model are frozen, and only the GVP layers for structure and surface graphs are trainable.
we use the average length (400 AAs) of all ProteinGym sequences for estimation.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: A non-redundant subset of CATH v4.3.0: 30,948 experimental structures with under 40% sequence identity. ESM-2-650M weights are reused, not retrained.

quotes.text: Our models are pre-trained on a non-redundant subset of CATH v4.3.0 dataset (CC BY 4.0 license) [30],
which contains 30,948 experimental structures with less than 40% sequence identity.

notes: S2F, S2F-MSA, S3F and S3F-MSA share one paper, repository and Zenodo record; shared files were fetched once and copied into each folder. parameters in structured is the trainable count from the paper's Table 1, read from the pdftotext -layout file; ESM-2-650M is frozen and not included. The paper PDF is kept as artifacts/paper.pdf; the two text files are its text layers. The Zenodo JSON is not marked for storage because no saved file states a licence for the metadata itself. S3F-MSA has no checkpoint or code of its own, but the record describes a distinct scored method, so a spec without a run guide was written rather than a stub.
no_run_guide_reason: No S3F-MSA checkpoint or ensembling script is released. The repository evaluates S3F only; the EVE half of the ensemble and the z-score combination are described in the paper but not provided as code. See the S3F page for running S3F.
